Target audience: High school students or beginners in STEM

Section: section_1 — What is a Vector? (Intuitive Concept)

Lecture lines:
Scalars have only magnitude.
Vectors add direction to magnitude.
Vectors act like arrows in space.

Planned animations:
Display an arrow on screen. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Show the arrow moving from the origin. Color: #FF00FF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Display a second identical vector alongside. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'Vector u'.

Section: section_2 — Visualizing Vector Addition

Lecture lines:
Place vectors tip-to-tail.
The resultant connects start to finish.
Addition is commutative.

Planned animations:
Show vectors u and v head-to-tail. Color: #00FFFF, #FF00FF. Label: 'u', 'v'.
Draw the resultant vector from origin. Color: #FFFF00. Label: 'u + v'.
Animate vector u sliding to connect to vector v. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'u + v'.

Section: section_3 — The Components of a Vector

Lecture lines:
Break vectors into x and y.
Use i and j basis units.
Combine them to form vectors.

Planned animations:
Draw grid lines on background. Color: #333333.
Place vector v onto the grid. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Project vector v onto X and Y axes. Color: #FF0000, #00FF00. Labels: 'vx', 'vy'.

Section: section_4 — Scaling Vectors (Scalar Multiplication)

Lecture lines:
Scalars scale the vector's length.
Direction remains the same.
Negative scalars reverse the direction.

Planned animations:
Display vector v. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Animate stretching vector v by 2. Color: #00FF00. Label: '2v'.
Animate shrinking vector v by 0.5. Color: #FF0000. Label: '0.5v'.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Vectors model motion and space.
They power physics engines.
Fundamental to modern navigation.

Planned animations:
Display a collection of vectors together. Color: #FFFFFF. Labels: 'Set of Vectors'.
Highlight a single vector rotating. Color: #FFFF00. Label: 'Rotation'.
Flash all vectors simultaneously for final impact. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'System'.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
